**In brief**
- Lord Fowler (Conservative backbencher) argued on 7 March 2012 for independent decisions on media takeovers, as when he said "our aim should be to have safeguards that prevent any one organisation owning a disproportionate share of the British media and that final decisions on media mergers and takeovers should be taken independently, not by Ministers" [Source 12].
- Labour's frontbench spokesperson pressed for stronger regulatory powers, as when Baroness Jones of Whitchurch asked whether the Government should be "taking urgent action to strengthen Ofcom's powers to intervene where it has doubts about whether UK broadcasting licence holders are fit and proper persons" [Source 7].
- The Government minister set out a process rather than a position, as when Baroness Garden of Frognal said the Government would outline "high-level thinking on media ownership and plurality in the forthcoming communications Green Paper" [Source 6].

**Government (Liberal Democrat Lords spokesperson) – deferring to forthcoming reviews**

Baroness Garden of Frognal answered by pointing to pending work, as when she said the Government had "commissioned a report from Ofcom on these matters to be delivered in June 2012" [Source 6].
- She said the Leveson inquiry would also report on matters related to media plurality and any recommendations would be considered as part of the communications review [Source 6].
- Asked about stronger Ofcom powers, she said "there are competing views on this issue" and "we really cannot pre-empt the decisions" on ongoing investigations [Source 8].

**Labour – pressing for action on News International**

Labour peers tied plurality to News International, as when Baroness Jones of Whitchurch referred to "the catalogue of News International's misdeeds spreading more widely" [Source 7] and called the matter "a matter of urgency now" [Source 7].
- Lord Soley (Labour backbencher) asked whether "there would actually be more media diversity now if, instead of closing down the News of the World, News International had taken responsibility" [Source 9].

**Conservative and Crossbench backbenchers – ownership and independence**

Backbenchers raised ownership concerns, as when Lord Fowler recalled that "last July we were only days away from News Corp's bid for BSkyB being waved through" [Source 12].
- Baroness O'Neill of Bengarve (Crossbench) asked what the Government would do "in the event that Mr James Murdoch or, indeed, News International, decides to dispose of further UK newspaper titles" [Source 11], and whether they would be content with Chinese or Qatari ownership.
